claim_ceiling: A collection-count attribution measured in THIS environment at THIS root. It says nothing about pass/fail (no suite was run), nothing about any other environment, and nothing about any frozen bar. It measures which commit moved a collected count, which is a statement about the git history of this repository, not about product behaviour.

method.attribution_rule: a step's delta is the change in the whole-suite collected count across that commit, attributed to the modules git says it added or modified
method.head_and_working_tree: the range ends at a COMMIT, so the committed decomposition always closes on its own; the uncommitted working tree is measured separately and attributed to the modules `git status` reports, because a cycle's in-flight tests are not a commit and must never be silently folded into a committed range's arithmetic
method.measurement: pytest --collect-only -q (collection only; NO suite run, no pass/fail claim)
method.per_module: per-module counts are collected AFTER the commit; a module that cannot be collected in this environment is recorded as an error, never as 0
method.step_selection: git log --reverse base..head, keeping only commits whose name-status touches product/tests/; a commit that touches no test module cannot move a collected count and is skipped with this rule stated rather than silently
method.worktree_lifecycle: one detached worktree per measured commit under a temporary directory, removed and pruned in a finally block; nothing outside it is touched
